terms.gloss: a flake of snow, a tuft of snow
terms.comment: A description of ours. Floccus is a tuft or flock of wool (Varro, Celsus), and the authors liken falling snow to wool: Martial calls it a fleece of silent waters, and the psalm says that God gives snow like wool. We have found no ancient or modern word for a single snowflake in Lewis & Short, the loci collections, Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Of the snow falling, the plain ningit or nix cadit is usually enough.

phrases.latin: Ecce floccī nivis! Linguā ūnum cape.
phrases.english: Look, snowflakes! Catch one on your tongue.

phrases.latin: Aspice quam dēnsum tacitārum vellus aquārum dēfluat in voltūs Caesaris inque sinūs.
phrases.english: See how thick the fleece of silent waters falls on Caesar’s face and into his lap.

phrases.latin: Quī dat nivem sīcut lānam; nebulam sīcut cinerem spargit.
phrases.english: Who gives snow like wool, and scatters mist like ashes.

sources: Lewis & Short: floccus · Lewis & Short: nix
